PROP-P10-POTTS-34.statement: Potts 2007 sec.2.6: for expressives, repetition leads to strengthening rather than redundancy; ex. (34) accumulates standalone Damn plus prenominal damn (mixed positions).
PROP-P10-POTTS-34.note: One proposition and one mixed-position example. Five assertions pass on it; five adjacent-repetition miscodings of it are rejected. Not two within-use effects.

PROP-P10-QUIRK-EMPH.statement: Quirk et al. 1985 note [b] pp.982-983: expressions like yes, no, well, OK, all right are often repeated for emphasis (cf. 18.58).
PROP-P10-QUIRK-EMPH.note: Effect (emphasis/strengthening) explicit. Pattern unspecified: 18.58 covers adjacent reiteration and non-adjacent reinforcement.

PROP-P10-DING-HUH.statement: Dingemanse 2024 transcript token with adjacent Huh? Huh? occurrence; no effect stated.
PROP-P10-DING-HUH.note: Occurrence evidence only. No effect dimension may be derived from it.

PROP-P11-CGEL-SCOPE.statement: CGEL Ch.15 p.1360: supplements do not fall within the scope of negatives in the anchor.
PROP-P11-CGEL-SCOPE.note: Brett scope ruling 2026-11-04: CGEL Ch.15 p.1360 supplement properties are general to supplements, interjections included, despite preceding subsection (i). Inherited by DAMN_REACT, OUCH, WOW. One proposition, one outcome direction, no within-target contrast.
